West edge: Dar Masalit is 'bounded to the west by Wadai… to the east by the Fur', and Dar Tama 'has always been a bone of contention between the Sultans of Wadai and Darfur' (MacMichael I pp.85–86). So the core stops east of Dar Masalit/Tama, which should be drawn as a contested zone (geometry not yet drawn). VERIFY removed. W edge pulled east from 22.4–22.6°E to 23.0–23.1°E so the core lies east of the Dar Masalit/Dar Tama frontier band on the War Office 1904 overlay (OVERLAY_CHECK.md), per the Historian's ruling 'core edge east of Dar Masalit and Dar Tama' (MacMichael I pp.85–86); Dar Masalit stays a contested point.

properties.basis: West borderland of Ali Dinar's restored sultanate: Dar Masalit is 'bounded to the west by Wadai… to the north by Dars Tama and Kimr, and to the east by the Fur', and Dar Tama 'has always been a bone of contention between the Sultans of Wadai and Darfur' (MacMichael I pp.85–86); of Dar Masalit itself: 'Like Dar Tama it has always been a bone of contention as between Wadai and Darfur' (ibid.); the sultanate was 'nominally tributary to, but effectively independent of, the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan' (GHA VII p.283). Shown as a single APPROXIMATE point at the Dar Masalit anchor; no Dar Tama point because no sourced historical coordinate was found (Wikidata Q2439275 is the modern Chadian Dar Tama Department, not used).
